blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — Nine of 11 major irrigation systems monitored by the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) in Eastern Visayas have recorded below-normal water levels, prompting the agency to adjust water delivery schedules to farmers. In an advisory issued on Sept. 11, the NIA said the declining water levels were brought about by the prevailing weather conditions and appealed to farmers served by the affected irrigation systems to cooperate with the adjusted irrigation schedules. The agency said the measure was necessary to ensure that the available water supply would be distributed efficiently and reach as many rice fields as possible. […]...
